core.text: Commit to the working hypothesis that fixed 300 rpm bulk rotation for 60 seconds can repeatedly achieve the bounded final-vial target without requiring stable side images. One stipulated trial achieved approximately 2.4 percent spread despite earlier optical spreads above 4 percent. This defeats universal necessity of the preferred dependency in this case; repeatability and causal sufficiency remain hypotheses.

Proposed operating construction: run up to six fresh, rinsed-vessel trials within 90 minutes using 150 mL water and 0.30 mL dye, one bottle, fixed addition location and locked camera. Command 300 rpm for exactly 60 seconds, then stop without feedback-driven restart. Log five-second optical checks without letting them control stirring. Begin three 1 mL depth samples at second 120, finish within ten seconds, and alternate sampling order between paired trials. Keep the spill tray in use and stop for escaping liquid. Record references, raw vial readings, normalized spread, commanded duration and every target failure. Success requires vial spread at most 4 percent.

residue.text: The 900 rpm fluctuations, depression and transient specks remain unresolved. Agitation-renewed optical disturbance and its proposed feedback loop are hypotheses, not observed mechanisms; bubbles cannot be identified with these resources. Do not make their identification a prerequisite for the chosen fixed-speed construction.

The solitary lower-speed success may reflect sampling disturbance or an exceptional trial. Matched 900 rpm final-vial results and total preferred stirring duration are absent, so comparative uniformity and time savings are unknown. Reference repeatability is not concentration calibration; actual rpm is unverified. Generalization beyond this recipe and bounded sample proxy is unsupported.

tension.account_a: Working hypothesis: fixed 300 rpm rotation for 60 seconds reliably reaches the bounded final-vial criterion independently of optical stop-rule satisfaction.
tension.account_b: Incompatible rival hypothesis: fixed 300 rpm rotation for 60 seconds generally leaves depth gradients; the single successful sample set was exceptional or sampling-mediated.
tension.prediction_a: Repeated fresh trials using the precommitted construction will yield final-vial spreads at most 4 percent, including trials whose early optical checks exceed 4 percent.
tension.prediction_b: The same repeated construction will frequently yield final-vial spreads above 4 percent; systematic dependence on sampling order would further support sampling-mediated success. These are predictions, and failure would not prove 900 rpm necessary.
